items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: I recall they had all the kids like, Kid Punch, Kid Rene, Kid Tibor Remy, Kid Clayton, Chris Kelly, Kid Shots, and many, many others.

ctx.x: Yeah, I like the automobile like that now. No, you didn't like that. Everything was quiet, you see. It was wonderful, I'm telling you. It was wonderful. Now, we had some wonderful bands. I could name you some of those bands, let's see. They had the Golden Leaf Band. They had the Maple Leaf Band. They had the Supreme Band. They had the Crescent City Band. They had the Superior Band. They had the Olympic Band. They had the Eagle Band. They had the Eagle Band. All those bands. And later on they had, I recall they…
Why did they call them Kid?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: And he joined my band and played with me.

ctx.x: I thought maybe he played with you in those days, in years gone by. Before? Yeah, with Eddie Marsh and George E. Bush.

Yeah, that's when he played with me. That's when he played with me, before I ever left here. He had been to Chicago with Lewis and he said something, he got slow in his foot or something, I don't know what was wrong. But he left Chicago and come here, see. And he joined my band and played with me. Until one night we was playing with some white boys back, way back off Porter Street. Back, I believe Galvis, somewhere around that day. And Paul must have thought he was still up north, you know, trying to flag them…
But he know it better, yeah.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: He's on the order of this Paul Barbarian, Paul Barbarian. He just like him.

ctx.x: That was a little kid. He's a good drummer but he never had no idea about, you know, running no band. But he didn't put the band in his name, but he's a real good little drummer. He's on the order of this Paul Barbarian, Paul Barbarian. He just like him. Well who, uh... Who did run that band? Put that down, Lionel.
Who did run that band? What band?

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: I played a lot of jobs up there with Kid Punch's band, Irish Channel.

ctx.x: What did you do when the fight stopped? When the fight stopped?

Just get out the way, move out the way. Try and protect my drums and get out the way. Well, they never bothered us. I mean, they'd be fighting amongst themselves. But they was good people, though. They were really nice. I played a lot of jobs up there with Kid Punch's band, Irish Channel. Kid Punch had so much work. At that time, I had to carry my drums, you know, from down here and all the way up to the Irish Channel. You see, you wouldn't lie on a street car. Or you'd catch a ride, somebody, you know, with a…
When did Chani play with Punch? Before you or after?
